## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nandakapetavatthu* (Pv 38, also cited as 4.3) is a verse narrative within the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [Norman 1983]. In this text, a ghost gives counsel to a king concerning the severe hazards of wrong views and urges him to take refuge in the Triple Gem. Based on internal chronological clues, K. R. Norman highlights that the poem refers to Pingalaka, a king of Surattha, who is explained by the commentator Dhammapāla as having reigned contemporary with the Mauryan emperor Dhammāsoka two centuries after the Buddha's death [Norman 1983]. Consequently, the composition of the *Nandakapetavatthu* represents a relatively late layer within the Pali canon, matching the timeline assigned to certain late verses in the *Theragāthā* and *Therīgāthā* [Norman 1983].
